newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Oct 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Oct 14.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Monday:
- U.S. President Bill Clinton is in "very good" health and has not suffered any serious ailments apart from weight, allergies and hoarseness.
- General Abdul Rashid Dostrum is gaining popularity in northern Afghanistan as he forms an alliance with other rebels to resist the Muslim fundamentalist of the Taliban movement.
- U.S. executives at companies going bankrupt manage to preserve their pension plans, while managers see the money in their plans dwindle away.

- Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole's campaign has tentatively decided to invest more resources in California as Clinton leads in public opinion polls in almost every part of the country weeks before elections.
